messages:
alex: Heads-up — we keep seeing variance in 429 payloads from routed vs quota enforcement. Users get inconsistent retry guidance in the SDK/console. Need a short policy.
marie: Agreed. Can someone map current sources? I think 429s come from: per-route rate limiter, tenant global quota, and gateway backpressure.
tom: +1. Also some 429s are synthetic: our fallback admission controller emits 429 when queueing is disabled. Those don't mean 'try again later' necessarily.
jasmine: For console UX, we should show a badge that says either 'Rate limit' or 'Capacity throttle' based on provenance. That way users don't assume quota burn.
alex: Good. Suggestion: add a header X-Redwood-Signal: quota|route|backpressure|admission and include a human-readable hint field: Retry-After or Retry-Hint (short text). SDKs can map that to -> RetryAdvice.
marie: I like the header idea but we must be careful about leaking internal signals. Are these safe to expose to customers?
dan: We're ok exposing provenance if wording is consumer friendly. e.g. don't leak implementation words like 'admission controller'. Use external phrasing: 'temporary capacity limit' vs 'per-route rate limit'.
tom: Implementation note: adv header could be set by the final router service. We already attach telemetry tags; reusing them to set header is straightforward. Need to update edge code paths and tests.
sre-bot: deploy requested by tom:infra-team at 1715151600 — rolling patch to edge to add X-Redwood-Signal (staging only).
jasmine: Another UX: console should surface a single line in the request detail: "Throttle cause: <friendly text>" and link to runbook when it's quota-related. Runbook link only for quota or billing-related causes.
alex: Also decide status code mapping for capacity vs internal errors. Should capacity/backpressure be 429 or 503? Currently some capacity throttles return 429, others 503. Inconsistency breaks client retry heuristics.
mdan: (typo) dan: I'd prefer 429 for client-triggered limits (rate/quota) and 503 for system capacity problems where we recommend exponential backoff + jitter.
marie: That split makes sense. So policy: 429 = client-limited (quota, rate); 503 = transient capacity/fallbacks. Where we return 429 but it's actually capacity (legacy), we migrate to 503 and include a Deprecated header for a release window.
tom: We should add telemetry tag 'signal_class=client|system' and ensure alerts + dashboards use that. Then migration won't blindside SRE.
jasmine: For console copy, proposed phrasing: "429 — request rate exceeded. Reduce request frequency or contact support to increase quota. See runbook." "503 — temporary capacity issue. Retry with backoff. If persistent, contact support." Thoughts?
dan: Add small retry hints: 429 shows 'suggested wait: <Retry-After if available> or "try in a few seconds"'. 503 shows 'we recommend exponential backoff, starting at 1s'.
sre-bot: note: alert rule 'high-503-rate' will be updated to include signal_class=system at 1715151650.
alex: Next steps: 1) infra: add X-Redwood-Signal header and signal_class telemetry (tom). 2) SDK: map header -> structured RetryAdvice and surface to users (marie). 3) Console: show badge + runbook link for quota (jasmine). 4) Docs + release notes with migration windows (dan). Deadline: staging rollout by EOW?
marie: EOW is tight but ok for staging. Will prioritize SDK mapping after header exists.
tom: I'll open a PR and ping infra on-call for review. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/edge/pull/432 (staging only).
jasmine: I'll draft console copy and wireframes in Figma — will drop link here when ready.
alex: Great. If anyone disagrees with status-code split speak now. Otherwise I'll write the RFC snippet for eng-platform and sync with legal on wording.
dan: No objections from me.
marie: 👍 small nit: include examples in RFC of header values and sample SDK mapping pseudocode.
alex: Will do. Thanks all.
